panels.title: Accumulation — the corpus grows
panels.description: Wave B: memory-write and chunks-indexed counters (M2) must exist before this row is populated. Currently empty — accumulation panels gated on new OTel instrumentation.

panels.title: Recall Hit-Rate
panels.description: Rolling ratio of recall calls that returned at least one match, over a 1-hour window: sum(increase(audittrace_recall_total{hit="true"}[1h])) / sum(increase(audittrace_recall_total[1h])). Rendered with min-interval ≥ 15m and connected-nulls OFF — gaps (hours with no recalls) render as absence, never interpolated. Companion stat (24h hit-rate + total recall count) is shown as a separate stat panel below. This panel proxies 'the corpus is being used usefully'; token-level causal influence (recall → output quality) is out of scope. Every ratio exposes its denominator (total recall count). Labels: {source, collection, hit}. No PII.

panels.title: Recall Hit-Rate — 24h summary
panels.description: Companion stat for the Recall Hit-Rate timeseries: 24-hour hit-rate + total recall count (denominator). Always shown together so a high hit-rate on n=3 reads as n=3, not as a strong signal. Headline: 24h hit-rate %; secondary: total recall count (denominator). This proxies 'the corpus is being used usefully' — token-level causal influence (recall → output quality) is out of scope. Labels: {source, collection, hit}. No PII.

panels.title: Results per Recall — p50 / p95 by collection
panels.description: p50 and p95 of true-candidate count (SearchPage.total) returned per recall call, per collection, from the audittrace_recall_results histogram. Rising p50 with stable hit-rate = richer corpus serving broader queries; p95 pinned at the retrieval cap = the length-cap boundary is being hit. Interpretation: this proxies 'the corpus is serving varied queries' — token-level causal influence (recall → output quality) is out of scope. Source: audittrace_recall_results histogram (histogram_quantile over _bucket). Labels: {source, collection, hit}. No PII.

panels.title: Recall Calls by Collection — 24h counts (governance view)
panels.description: Stacked 24-hour recall counts by collection, not ops/s — governance wants 'which collections were consulted and how often', not per-second rates that render as invisible spikes. Uses increase(...[24h]) for cumulative counts. The source label (tool vs backoffice) is available as a second grouping: tool recalls are agent in-process reads (e.g. via the recall_* tool), backoffice recalls are human reads via the REST API. Every recall call left an audited tool_calls row (ADR-029 end-to-end traceability). Labels: {source, collection, hit}. No PII.

panels.title: Governance & Health — Memory Read REST Calls
panels.description: Live HTTP metrics for memory read routes (GET requests). Zeros stay visible — an episodic read count of 0 is a finding (agents not consulting episodic memory via REST), not noise. This row is the boundary where the learning dashboard ends and the security/audit view begins.

panels.title: Memory Reads by Route — 24h total (GET)
panels.description: 24-hour totals for GET requests to memory read routes. Zeros stay visible — an episodic read count of 0 is a governance finding (agents not consulting episodic memory via REST), not noise. Before v2 ships, confirm the /memory/episodic* zero is real usage (not a route-label mismatch). If real, that's a legitimate item for the agent-charter loop (why do agents never read episodic via REST?). Source: http_server_request_duration_seconds_count. No PII.

panels.title: Memory Read Status — by response code (GET)
panels.description: 24-hour counts of HTTP response codes for GET requests to memory read routes. Expected 401 sources: expired tokens from scheduled probes, stale JWTs from previous sessions. A sudden spike in 401/403 is a security/governance signal — cross-reference with the (future) security dashboard. This panel is the boundary where the learning dashboard ends and the security/audit view begins. Source: http_server_request_duration_seconds_count grouped by http_response_status_code. No PII.
